assessment.nobel_worthiness: Gut-hormone physiology (proglucagon-derived GLP-1 as an incretin and satiety signal) turned into incretin therapies that have changed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Originality, mechanistic clarity and a very large, durable clinical impact together make this a leading candidate.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, receptor actions, GLP-2) and Mojsov (identification of the active form of GLP-1) form a plausible trio on the supplied names. Knudsen's contribution is drug development in industry and would be hard to fit within three places; other early contributors (for example Habener) are not in the supplied credit and I am not certain how credit should be distributed.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by decades of independent physiology and multiple large outcome trials; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely given the ongoing clinical impact.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among early GLP-1 characterization, pharmacology and drug development is contested and the supplied list may be incomplete.
The long-term safety profile of incretin therapies is still accumulating, though this is unlikely to affect the prize case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new class of organelle-to-nucleus signaling and a general principle of proteostasis, with relevance to secretory-cell biology, metabolism, neurodegeneration and cancer. The discovery is original, mechanistically elegant and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the two investigators who elucidated the Ire1-Hac1/XBP1 signaling pathway, so a two-person configuration is clean and well supported by the supplied credit; I have not independently verified the details of earlier yeast contributions.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed across yeast and mammals, with decades of follow-up and established links to disease; timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Clinical translation (for example ISRIB or UPR modulators) is still early, so impact is mainly conceptual.
Whether other contributors, such as those who defined the PERK and ATF6 branches, merit consideration is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced curative responses in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality. The concept is original and the clinical impact is clear and lasting; it is also expanding toward autoimmune disease.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation CAR design with costimulation) and June (clinical translation, durable remissions) are central. Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T cell trials; his inclusion versus other CAR pioneers (such as Eshhar) is a judgment call that I cannot fully resolve.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent approvals and long-term follow-up support the findings, though durability data and safety issues (toxicity, secondary malignancy) are still maturing.
uncertainties: Attribution is complicated by earlier chimeric receptor work not in the supplied credit.
Long-term remission rates and toxicity data continue to evolve.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that BCL-2 acts by blocking cell death rather than driving proliferation redefined oncogene action and established control of apoptosis as a cancer mechanism, leading to BH3 mimetics such as venetoclax. High conceptual and clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned and characterized the BCL-2 gene and its translocation, and Vaux showed its survival function in cells; Strasser contributed substantially to the later pathway. A trio of Cory, Adams and Vaux is plausible, but the allocation among Vaux, Strasser and others (also the Korsmeyer and Tsujimoto work, not in the credited list) is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across independent labs, with an approved targeted therapy and long clinical experience; recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Contributions of researchers outside the supplied credit (for example Korsmeyer, Tsujimoto) complicate a fair configuration.
Apoptosis was recognized in 2002, so originality of the broader theme must be argued on the cancer-therapy link.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defining the thymus-dependent T-cell and bursa-dependent B-cell lineages is a foundational insight of adaptive immunity, underlying vaccination, immunodeficiency diagnosis and immunotherapy. Originality and lasting scientific importance are very high.
assessment.attribution: Miller (thymus function and T cells) and Cooper (B-cell lineage, with Good and Peterson) are the two supplied names. The attribution is natural for a two-person prize, although Robert Good's role is not in the list and it is a limitation.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is thoroughly confirmed and textbook; recognition is, if anything, overdue, with the laureates now very elderly.
uncertainties: Time pressure given the age of the investigators.
Credit for the original bursa experiments (Glick, Good) falls outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated ion channels used to control defined cell types transformed causal neuroscience and are entering clinical use (vision restoration). The channelrhodopsin discovery and its neuronal application are original, with broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its application in neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth, and Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted approach) are separable, which makes a three-person configuration difficult and contested. A Hegemann, Nagel and Deisseroth set tries to cover discovery and neuronal use, at the cost of leaving out Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and technically mature, but the contribution is a tool rather than a disease mechanism; clinical outcomes are still emerging.
uncertainties: Contested priority and a compound discovery whose parts need different recognition.
Six credited names against a three-person limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and its role as a central regulator of growth and nutrient signaling is a major conceptual advance with relevance to cancer, metabolism, immunology and aging.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically in yeast and is the clearest decisive contributor. Schreiber contributed the chemical biology of FKBP12-rapamycin and mTOR target identification, while Sabatini's role is later mammalian pathway work and I would be cautious about including him; the credit remains partly unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is strongly confirmed by many independent groups, and rapalogs are clinically used; recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber and others (Sabatini, Sabers, Heitman) is unresolved.
Clinical impact of rapalogs is narrower than the biological importance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating that TNF is a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis changed treatment of chronic inflammatory disease and opened the field of cytokine-targeted biologics. The translational step was original and the impact is large and durable.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini identified TNF as a driver in synovial cultures and led the first clinical trials, so a two-person configuration is clear on the supplied names. Others contributed to TNF biology and antibody development (for example Cerami, Vilcek, Kollias), who are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many trials and decades of use, with biosimilars; recognition is mature, though the Lasker already honored this.
uncertainties: Whether the discovery is judged as basic mechanism or clinical translation, and the strength of the conceptual novelty relative to the antibody engineering.
Credit for TNF biology outside the supplied names.
